holidays.name: Wright Brothers Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the nerdy bicycle mechanics who convinced humanity that falling with style could be called flying. Aviation fans gather to fly kites, build paper airplanes, and look wistfully at the sky.
holidays.origin: On December 17, 1903, Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first powered, controlled airplane flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. In 1963, Congress and President Lyndon B. Johnson officially designated the day as Wright Brothers Day.
holidays.funFact: Orville's first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, which is shorter than the wingspan of a Boeing 747.

holidays.name: Maple Syrup Day
holidays.description: A sticky-sweet celebration of the golden liquid that turns plain pancakes into a personality. Fans drizzle it on waffles, bacon, oatmeal, and brave experiments like ice cream and cocktails.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday popular with syrup lovers and food bloggers, and it shows up on many food-holiday calendars. It honors the tradition of tapping maple trees, which long predates European settlers and was practiced by Indigenous peoples of North America.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 40 gallons of maple sap to boil down into just one gallon of maple syrup.

holidays.name: Saturnalia
holidays.description: The ancient Roman festival of feasting, gift-giving, gambling, and general mischief, where social rules were flipped upside down. Masters served their slaves, everybody wore silly hats, and a mock king was chosen to preside over the party.
holidays.origin: Saturnalia began as a Roman farming festival honoring Saturn, the god of agriculture, and was traditionally held on December 17. Over time it grew into a week-long celebration that likely influenced later winter holiday traditions.
holidays.funFact: Romans exchanged small gifts during Saturnalia, such as candles and little clay figurines, and the festival is often cited as an ancestor of modern Christmas customs.

holidays.name: Underdog Day
holidays.description: A day for cheering on the long shots, the little guys, and the cartoon dog in a cape who saves the day while speaking in rhyme. Fans celebrate perseverance and rooting for the one nobody expects to win.
holidays.origin: The observance is tied to the animated superhero Underdog, whose TV series debuted in October 1964, and it has since been adopted by fans on various holiday calendars. Its date is a nod to the series' cultural legacy and to the general spirit of backing the underdog.
holidays.funFact: Underdog's secret identity is the meek, mild-mannered shoeshine boy Shoeshine Boy, and he gets his powers from a Super Energy Pill he keeps in a ring.

holidays.name: International Day to End Violence Against Sex Workers
holidays.description: A serious awareness day that brings attention to the safety, rights, and dignity of sex workers around the world. Supporters hold vigils and events, and advocate for policy changes.
holidays.origin: The day began in 2003 as a memorial and day of action after the Green River Killer case, with activist Annie Sprinkle and the Sex Workers Outreach Project USA leading the call for recognition. It has since grown into an international observance.
holidays.funFact: Participants often use red umbrellas as a symbol of resistance to discrimination, a tradition that dates back to a 2001 protest at the Venice Biennale.
